passages.text: This is what the LORD says: “Behold, I will stir up against Babylon and against the people of Leb-kamai the spirit of a destroyer.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD speaks with authority.
The LORD says this.
I will act against Babylon.
I will act against the people who live in Leb-kamai.
I will stir up a spirit of destruction against them.
This spirit will bring ruin.
passages.original: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְנִי֙ מֵעִ֣יר עַל־ בָּבֶ֔ל וְאֶל־ יֹשְׁבֵ֖י לֵ֣ב קָמָ֑י ר֖וּחַ מַשְׁחִֽית׃

passages.text: I will send strangers to Babylon to winnow her and empty her land; for they will come against her from every side in her day of disaster.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks about Babylon.
The LORD will send strangers to Babylon.
These strangers will winnow Babylon.
They will empty Babylon’s land.
They will come against Babylon from every side.
They will come on Babylon’s day of disaster.
passages.original: וְשִׁלַּחְתִּ֨י לְבָבֶ֤ל׀ זָרִים֙ וְזֵר֔וּהָ וִיבֹקְק֖וּ אֶת־ אַרְצָ֑הּ כִּֽי־ הָי֥וּ עָלֶ֛יהָ מִסָּבִ֖יב בְּי֥וֹם רָעָֽה׃

passages.text: Do not let the archer bend his bow or put on his armor. Do not spare her young men; devote all her army to destruction!
passages.sermon:
God speaks about Babylon.
God commands the attackers.
Do not let the archer bend his bow.
Do not let the archer put on his armor.
Do not spare Babylon’s young men.
Destroy all her army.
passages.original: אֶֽל־ יִדְרֹ֤ךְ הַדֹּרֵךְ֙ קַשְׁתּ֔וֹ וְאֶל־ יִתְעַ֖ל בְּסִרְיֹנ֑וֹ וְאַֽל־ תַּחְמְלוּ֙ אֶל־ בַּ֣חֻרֶ֔יהָ הַחֲרִ֖ימוּ כָּל־ צְבָאָֽהּ׃

passages.text: And they will fall slain in the land of the Chaldeans, and pierced through in her streets.
passages.sermon: Many people will die in the land of the Chaldeans.\r\nEnemies will kill them in the streets.\r\nTheir bodies will lie where they fall.
passages.original: וְנָפְל֥וּ חֲלָלִ֖ים בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּ֑ים וּמְדֻקָּרִ֖ים בְּחוּצוֹתֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: For Israel and Judah have not been abandoned by their God, the LORD of Hosts, though their land is full of guilt before the Holy One of Israel.”
passages.sermon:
Israel and Judah belong to God.
God is the LORD of Hosts.
God has not abandoned Israel and Judah.
Their land is full of guilt.
The Holy One of Israel sees their guilt.
passages.original: כִּ֠י לֹֽא־ אַלְמָ֨ן יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל וִֽיהוּדָה֙ מֵֽאֱלֹהָ֔יו מֵֽיְהוָ֖ה צְבָא֑וֹת כִּ֤י אַרְצָם֙ מָלְאָ֣ה אָשָׁ֔ם מִקְּד֖וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Flee from Babylon! Escape with your lives! Do not be destroyed in her punishment. For this is the time of the LORD’s vengeance; He will pay her what she deserves.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD of Hosts.
God is bringing vengeance.
Babylon is under God's judgment.
Flee from Babylon.
Save your life.
Do not be caught in Babylon's punishment.
This is the time for the LORD to take revenge.
God will repay Babylon for her deeds.
passages.original: נֻ֣סוּ׀ מִתּ֣וֹךְ בָּבֶ֗ל וּמַלְּטוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ נַפְשׁ֔וֹ אַל־ תִּדַּ֖מּוּ בַּעֲוֺנָ֑הּ כִּי֩ עֵ֨ת נְקָמָ֥ה הִיא֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה גְּמ֕וּל ה֥וּא מְשַׁלֵּ֖ם לָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Babylon was a gold cup in the hand of the LORD, making the whole earth drunk. The nations drank her wine; therefore the nations have gone mad.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel and Judah.
The LORD holds power over all nations.
Babylon was like a gold cup in the hand of the LORD.
Babylon made the whole earth drunk.
The nations drank the wine from Babylon.
Because of this, the nations have gone mad.
passages.original: כּוֹס־ זָהָ֤ב בָּבֶל֙ בְּיַד־ יְהוָ֔ה מְשַׁכֶּ֖רֶת כָּל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ מִיֵּינָהּ֙ שָׁת֣וּ גוֹיִ֔ם עַל־ כֵּ֖ן יִתְהֹלְל֥וּ גוֹיִֽם׃

passages.text: Suddenly Babylon has fallen and been shattered. Wail for her; get her balm for her pain; perhaps she can be healed.
passages.sermon:
Babylon was a great and powerful city.
God judged Babylon for her sins.
Suddenly Babylon fell.
Babylon was shattered.
People mourned for Babylon.
They cried out in sorrow for her.
They tried to find balm to heal her pain.
They hoped Babylon could be healed.
passages.original: פִּתְאֹ֛ם נָפְלָ֥ה בָבֶ֖ל וַתִּשָּׁבֵ֑ר הֵילִ֣ילוּ עָלֶ֗יהָ קְח֤וּ צֳרִי֙ לְמַכְאוֹבָ֔הּ אוּלַ֖י תֵּרָפֵֽא׃

passages.text: “We tried to heal Babylon, but she could not be healed. Abandon her! Let each of us go to his own land, for her judgment extends to the sky and reaches to the clouds.”
passages.sermon:
Babylon was a powerful and wicked nation.
God judged Babylon because of her sins.
We tried to heal Babylon.
Babylon could not be healed.
Leave Babylon.
Each person should return to his own land.
Babylon’s judgment has reached up to the sky.
Her punishment rises as high as the clouds.
passages.original: רִפִּאנוּ אֶת־ בָּבֶל֙ וְלֹ֣א נִרְפָּ֔תָה עִזְב֕וּהָ וְנֵלֵ֖ךְ אִ֣ישׁ לְאַרְצ֑וֹ כִּֽי־ נָגַ֤ע אֶל־ הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ מִשְׁפָּטָ֔הּ וְנִשָּׂ֖א עַד־ שְׁחָקִֽים׃

passages.text: “The LORD has brought forth our vindication; come, let us tell in Zion what the LORD our God has accomplished.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is our God.
The LORD has shown that we are right.
The LORD has brought out our vindication.
Let us go to Zion.
Let us tell in Zion what the LORD has done.
Let us declare the works of the LORD our God.
passages.original: הוֹצִ֥יא יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־ צִדְקֹתֵ֑ינוּ בֹּ֚אוּ וּנְסַפְּרָ֣ה בְצִיּ֔וֹן אֶֽת־ מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: Sharpen the arrows! Fill the quivers! The LORD has aroused the spirit of the kings of the Medes, because His plan is aimed at Babylon to destroy her, for it is the vengeance of the LORD— vengeance for His temple.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD has a plan against Babylon.
The LORD wants to destroy Babylon.
The LORD seeks vengeance for His temple.
The LORD has stirred up the kings of the Medes.
The kings of the Medes will attack Babylon.
Sharpen the arrows.
Fill the quivers.
Prepare for battle against Babylon.
This is the LORD’s vengeance.
This is vengeance for His holy temple.
passages.original: הָבֵ֣רוּ הַחִצִּים֮ מִלְא֣וּ הַשְּׁלָטִים֒ הֵעִ֣יר יְהוָ֗ה אֶת־ ר֙וּחַ֙ מַלְכֵ֣י מָדַ֔י כִּֽי־ עַל־ בָּבֶ֥ל מְזִמָּת֖וֹ לְהַשְׁחִיתָ֑הּ כִּֽי־ נִקְמַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ הִ֔יא נִקְמַ֖ת הֵיכָלֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Raise a banner against the walls of Babylon; post the guard; station the watchmen; prepare the ambush. For the LORD has both devised and accomplished what He spoke against the people of Babylon.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD has power and authority.
Babylon is a great city with strong walls.
Raise a banner against the walls of Babylon.
Post the guard at their stations.
Station the watchmen to keep watch.
Prepare the ambush against the city.
The LORD made a plan against the people of Babylon.
The LORD has done what He said He would do against them.
passages.original: אֶל־ חוֹמֹ֨ת בָּבֶ֜ל שְׂאוּ־ נֵ֗ס הַחֲזִ֙יקוּ֙ הַמִּשְׁמָ֔ר הָקִ֙ימוּ֙ שֹֽׁמְרִ֔ים הָכִ֖ינוּ הָאֹֽרְבִ֑ים כִּ֚י גַּם־ זָמַ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה גַּם־ עָשָׂ֕ה אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־ דִּבֶּ֖ר אֶל־ יֹשְׁבֵ֥י בָבֶֽל׃

passages.text: You who dwell by many waters, rich in treasures, your end has come; the thread of your life is cut.
passages.sermon:
Babylon lives beside many waters.
Babylon has great wealth.
Babylon’s end has come.
God has cut the thread of Babylon’s life.
passages.original: שֹׁכַנְתִּי עַל־ מַ֣יִם רַבִּ֔ים רַבַּ֖ת אֽוֹצָרֹ֑ת בָּ֥א קִצֵּ֖ךְ אַמַּ֥ת בִּצְעֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: The LORD of Hosts has sworn by Himself: “Surely I will fill you up with men as with locusts, and they will shout in triumph over you.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is God.
He has all power and commands armies.
The LORD of Hosts made a promise by Himself.
He said, “I will fill you with men like locusts.
These men will cover you completely.
They will shout in triumph over you.”
passages.original: נִשְׁבַּ֛ע יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת בְּנַפְשׁ֑וֹ כִּ֣י אִם־ מִלֵּאתִ֤יךְ אָדָם֙ כַּיֶּ֔לֶק וְעָנ֥וּ עָלַ֖יִךְ הֵידָֽד׃ס

passages.text: The LORD made the earth by His power; He established the world by His wisdom and stretched out the heavens by His understanding.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is powerful.
The LORD made the earth by His power.
The LORD is wise.
The LORD established the world by His wisdom.
The LORD is full of understanding.
The LORD stretched out the heavens by His understanding.
passages.original: עֹשֵׂ֥ה אֶ֙רֶץ֙ בְּכֹח֔וֹ מֵכִ֥ין תֵּבֵ֖ל בְּחָכְמָת֑וֹ וּבִתְבוּנָת֖וֹ נָטָ֥ה שָׁמָֽיִם׃

passages.text: When He thunders, the waters in the heavens roar; He causes the clouds to rise from the ends of the earth. He generates the lightning with the rain and brings forth the wind from His storehouses.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the Creator of all things.
He is powerful and wise.
He makes the earth by His power.
He establishes the world by His wisdom.
He stretches out the heavens by His understanding.
When the LORD thunders, the waters in the heavens roar.
He causes clouds to rise from the ends of the earth.
He makes lightning with the rain.
He brings forth the wind from His storehouses.
passages.original: לְק֨וֹל תִּתּ֜וֹ הֲמ֥וֹן מַ֙יִם֙ בַּשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיַּ֥עַל נְשִׂאִ֖ים מִקְצֵה־ אָ֑רֶץ בְּרָקִ֤ים לַמָּטָר֙ עָשָׂ֔ה וַיֹּ֥צֵא ר֖וּחַ מֵאֹצְרֹתָֽיו׃

passages.text: Every man is senseless and devoid of knowledge; every goldsmith is put to shame by his idols. For his molten images are a fraud, and there is no breath in them.
passages.sermon:
Every person lacks understanding.
Every person has no true knowledge.
Every goldsmith feels shame because of his idols.
His idols are false.
His molten images are a lie.
These images have no breath in them.
These idols are lifeless.
passages.original: נִבְעַ֤ר כָּל־ אָדָם֙ מִדַּ֔עַת הֹבִ֥ישׁ כָּל־ צֹרֵ֖ף מִפָּ֑סֶל כִּ֛י שֶׁ֥קֶר נִסְכּ֖וֹ וְלֹא־ ר֥וּחַ בָּֽם׃

passages.text: They are worthless, a work to be mocked. In the time of their punishment they will perish.
passages.sermon:
Idols are worthless.
People made these idols.
People made them to deceive others.
God will punish these idols.
When God punishes them, they will perish.
passages.original: הֶ֣בֶל הֵ֔מָּה מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה תַּעְתֻּעִ֑ים בְּעֵ֥ת פְּקֻדָּתָ֖ם יֹאבֵֽדוּ׃

passages.text: The Portion of Jacob is not like these, for He is the Maker of all things, and of the tribe of His inheritance— the LORD of Hosts is His name.
passages.sermon:
The Portion of Jacob is not like these idols.
God is the Portion of Jacob.
God made all things.
God is the Maker of everything.
God chose Jacob’s tribe as His inheritance.
God’s name is the LORD of Hosts.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ כְאֵ֜לֶּה חֵ֣לֶק יַעֲק֗וֹב כִּֽי־ יוֹצֵ֤ר הַכֹּל֙ ה֔וּא וְשֵׁ֖בֶט נַחֲלָת֑וֹ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: “You are My war club, My weapon for battle. With you I shatter nations; with you I bring kingdoms to ruin.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His chosen instrument.
God calls this person His war club.
God says, "You are My weapon for battle."
God uses this person to shatter nations.
God uses this person to bring kingdoms to ruin.
passages.original: מַפֵּץ־ אַתָּ֣ה לִ֔י כְּלֵ֖י מִלְחָמָ֑ה וְנִפַּצְתִּ֤י בְךָ֙ גּוֹיִ֔ם וְהִשְׁחַתִּ֥י בְךָ֖ מַמְלָכֽוֹת׃

passages.text: With you I shatter the horse and rider; with you I shatter the chariot and driver.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His chosen instrument.
God calls this instrument His war club.
God uses this war club to destroy enemies.
God says, “With you I shatter the horse and its rider.”
God says, “With you I shatter the chariot and its driver.”
passages.original: וְנִפַּצְתִּ֣י בְךָ֔ ס֖וּס וְרֹֽכְב֑וֹ וְנִפַּצְתִּ֣י בְךָ֔ רֶ֖כֶב וְרֹכְבֽוֹ׃

passages.text: With you I shatter man and woman; with you I shatter the old man and the youth; with you I shatter the young man and the maiden.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His chosen instrument.
God calls this instrument His war club.
God uses this war club to destroy.
God says, "With you I shatter a man."
God says, "With you I shatter a woman."
God says, "With you I shatter an old man."
God says, "With you I shatter a youth."
God says, "With you I shatter a young man."
God says, "With you I shatter a maiden."
passages.original: וְנִפַּצְתִּ֤י בְךָ֙ אִ֣ישׁ וְאִשָּׁ֔ה וְנִפַּצְתִּ֥י בְךָ֖ זָקֵ֣ן וָנָ֑עַר וְנִפַּצְתִּ֣י בְךָ֔ בָּח֖וּר וּבְתוּלָֽה׃

passages.text: With you I shatter the shepherd and his flock; with you I shatter the farmer and his oxen; with you I shatter the governors and officials.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Babylon.
God uses Babylon as an instrument of judgment.
God says, "With you, I shatter the shepherd and his flock."
God says, "With you, I shatter the farmer and his oxen."
God says, "With you, I shatter the governors and officials."
passages.original: וְנִפַּצְתִּ֤י בְךָ֙ רֹעֶ֣ה וְעֶדְר֔וֹ וְנִפַּצְתִּ֥י בְךָ֖ אִכָּ֣ר וְצִמְדּ֑וֹ וְנִפַּצְתִּ֣י בְךָ֔ פַּח֖וֹת וּסְגָנִֽים׃

passages.text: Before your very eyes I will repay Babylon and all the dwellers of Chaldea for all the evil they have done in Zion,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD promises justice.
Babylon did evil in Zion.
The people of Chaldea also did evil in Zion.
The LORD will repay Babylon for their evil.
The LORD will repay all the dwellers of Chaldea for their evil.
The LORD will do this openly.
You will see the LORD repay them with your own eyes.
passages.original: וְשִׁלַּמְתִּ֨י לְבָבֶ֜ל וּלְכֹ֣ל׀ יוֹשְׁבֵ֣י כַשְׂדִּ֗ים אֵ֧ת כָּל־ רָעָתָ֛ם אֲשֶׁר־ עָשׂ֥וּ בְצִיּ֖וֹן לְעֵֽינֵיכֶ֑ם נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: “Behold, I am against you, O destroying mountain, you who devastate the whole earth, declares the LORD. I will stretch out My hand against you; I will roll you over the cliffs and turn you into a charred mountain.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD declares His judgment.
The LORD addresses the destroying mountain.
This mountain destroys the whole earth.
The LORD says, “I am against you.”
The LORD will stretch out His hand against the mountain.
The LORD will roll the mountain over the cliffs.
The LORD will make the mountain a charred mountain.
passages.original: הִנְנִ֨י אֵלֶ֜יךָ הַ֤ר הַמַּשְׁחִית֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה הַמַּשְׁחִ֖ית אֶת־ כָּל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וְנָטִ֨יתִי אֶת־ יָדִ֜י עָלֶ֗יךָ וְגִלְגַּלְתִּ֙יךָ֙ מִן־ הַסְּלָעִ֔ים וּנְתַתִּ֖יךָ לְהַ֥ר שְׂרֵפָֽה׃

passages.text: No one shall retrieve from you a cornerstone or a foundation stone, because you will become desolate forever,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD declares judgment against Babylon.
Babylon will become desolate forever.
No one will take a cornerstone from Babylon.
No one will take a foundation stone from Babylon.
Babylon will remain empty and ruined forever.
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ יִקְח֤וּ מִמְּךָ֙ אֶ֣בֶן לְפִנָּ֔ה וְאֶ֖בֶן לְמֽוֹסָד֑וֹת כִּֽי־ שִׁמְמ֥וֹת עוֹלָ֛ם תִּֽהְיֶ֖ה נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: “Raise a banner in the land! Blow the ram’s horn among the nations! Prepare the nations against her. Summon the kingdoms against her— Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz. Appoint a captain against her; bring up horses like swarming locusts.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people.
God commands them to act.
Raise a banner in the land.
Blow the ram’s horn among the nations.
Prepare the nations to fight against Babylon.
Summon the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz against her.
Appoint a captain to lead them.
Bring up horses against Babylon.
Let the horses come in great numbers, like swarming locusts.
passages.original: שְׂאוּ־ נֵ֣ס בָּאָ֗רֶץ תִּקְע֨וּ שׁוֹפָ֤ר בַּגּוֹיִם֙ קַדְּשׁ֤וּ עָלֶ֙יהָ֙ גּוֹיִ֔ם הַשְׁמִ֧יעוּ עָלֶ֛יהָ מַמְלְכ֥וֹת אֲרָרַ֖ט מִנִּ֣י וְאַשְׁכְּנָ֑ז פִּקְד֤וּ עָלֶ֙יהָ֙ טִפְסָ֔ר הַֽעֲלוּ־ ס֖וּס כְּיֶ֥לֶק סָמָֽר׃

passages.text: Prepare the nations for battle against her— the kings of the Medes, their governors and all their officials, and all the lands they rule.
passages.sermon:
God commands the nations to prepare for battle against Babylon.
The kings of the Medes must join the fight.
The governors of the Medes must also join.
All the officials of the Medes must join as well.
Every land ruled by the Medes must take part in the battle.
passages.original: קַדְּשׁ֨וּ עָלֶ֤יהָ גוֹיִם֙ אֶת־ מַלְכֵ֣י מָדַ֔י אֶת־ פַּחוֹתֶ֖יהָ וְאֶת־ כָּל־ סְגָנֶ֑יהָ וְאֵ֖ת כָּל־ אֶ֥רֶץ מֶמְשַׁלְתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The earth quakes and writhes because the LORD’s intentions against Babylon stand: to make the land of Babylon a desolation, without inhabitant.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD has decided to punish Babylon.
The LORD will make the land of Babylon empty.
No one will live there.
The earth shakes.
The earth trembles.
The earth feels pain.
This happens because the LORD’s plans against Babylon are certain.
passages.original: וַתִּרְעַ֥שׁ הָאָ֖רֶץ וַתָּחֹ֑ל כִּ֣י קָ֤מָה עַל־ בָּבֶל֙ מַחְשְׁב֣וֹת יְהוָ֔ה לָשׂ֞וּם אֶת־ אֶ֧רֶץ בָּבֶ֛ל לְשַׁמָּ֖ה מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵֽׁב׃

passages.text: The warriors of Babylon have stopped fighting; they sit in their strongholds. Their strength is exhausted; they have become like women. Babylon’s homes have been set ablaze, the bars of her gates are broken.
passages.sermon:
The warriors of Babylon have stopped fighting.
They sit in their strongholds.
Their strength is gone.
They have become like women.
Enemies have set Babylon’s homes on fire.
The bars of Babylon’s gates are broken.
passages.original: חָדְלוּ֩ גִבּוֹרֵ֨י בָבֶ֜ל לְהִלָּחֵ֗ם יָֽשְׁבוּ֙ בַּמְּצָד֔וֹת נָשְׁתָ֥ה גְבוּרָתָ֖ם הָי֣וּ לְנָשִׁ֑ים הִצִּ֥יתוּ מִשְׁכְּנֹתֶ֖יהָ נִשְׁבְּר֥וּ בְרִיחֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: One courier races to meet another, and messenger follows messenger, to announce to the king of Babylon that his city has been captured from end to end.
passages.sermon:
A courier runs quickly.
He runs to meet another courier.
A messenger follows after another messenger.
They go to the king of Babylon.
They bring news to the king.
They say his city has been captured.
The whole city is taken from one end to the other.
passages.original: רָ֤ץ לִקְרַאת־ רָץ֙ יָר֔וּץ וּמַגִּ֖יד לִקְרַ֣את מַגִּ֑יד לְהַגִּיד֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל כִּֽי־ נִלְכְּדָ֥ה עִיר֖וֹ מִקָּצֶֽה׃

passages.text: The fords have been seized, the marshes set on fire, and the soldiers are terrified.”
passages.sermon:
Babylon is under attack.
The enemy has taken control of the fords.
The enemy has set the marshes on fire.
The soldiers are terrified.
passages.original: וְהַמַּעְבָּר֣וֹת נִתְפָּ֔שׂוּ וְאֶת־ הָאֲגַמִּ֖ים שָׂרְפ֣וּ בָאֵ֑שׁ וְאַנְשֵׁ֥י הַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה נִבְהָֽלוּ׃ס

passages.text: For this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: “The Daughter of Babylon is like a threshing floor at the time it is trampled. In just a little while her harvest time will come.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is the God of Israel.
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
The LORD of Hosts says this about Babylon.
Babylon is like a daughter.
Babylon is like a threshing floor.
People trample the threshing floor at harvest time.
Soon, Babylon will be trampled.
Her time of harvest will come soon.
passages.original: כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בַּת־ בָּבֶ֕ל כְּגֹ֖רֶן עֵ֣ת הִדְרִיכָ֑הּ ע֣וֹד מְעַ֔ט וּבָ֥אָה עֵֽת־ הַקָּצִ֖יר לָֽהּ׃

passages.text: “Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has devoured me; he has crushed me. He has set me aside like an empty vessel; he has swallowed me like a monster; he filled his belly with my delicacies and vomited me out.
passages.sermon:
Nebuchadnezzar is the king of Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar has devoured me.
Nebuchadnezzar has crushed me.
He has set me aside like an empty vessel.
He has swallowed me like a monster.
He filled his belly with my delicacies.
He has vomited me out.
passages.original: אֲכָלָנוּ הֲמָמָנוּ נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֮ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶל֒ הִצִּיגָנוּ כְּלִ֣י רִ֔יק בְּלָעָנוּ כַּתַּנִּ֔ין מִלָּ֥א כְרֵשׂ֖וֹ מֵֽעֲדָנָ֑י הֱדִיחָנוּ׃

passages.text: May the violence done to me and to my flesh be upon Babylon,” says the dweller of Zion. “May my blood be on the dwellers of Chaldea,” says Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
The people of Zion speak.
They say, “Let the violence done to me fall on Babylon.”
Jerusalem speaks.
She says, “Let my blood be on the people of Chaldea.”
passages.original: חֲמָסִ֤י וּשְׁאֵרִי֙ עַל־ בָּבֶ֔ל תֹּאמַ֖ר יֹשֶׁ֣בֶת צִיּ֑וֹן וְדָמִי֙ אֶל־ יֹשְׁבֵ֣י כַשְׂדִּ֔ים תֹּאמַ֖ר יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס

passages.text: Therefore this is what the LORD says: “Behold, I will plead your case and take vengeance on your behalf; I will dry up her sea and make her springs run dry.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD speaks with authority.
The LORD says these words.
I will defend your cause.
I will take vengeance for you.
I will destroy Babylon’s sea.
I will make Babylon’s springs dry.
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְנִי־ רָב֙ אֶת־ רִיבֵ֔ךְ וְנִקַּמְתִּ֖י אֶת־ נִקְמָתֵ֑ךְ וְהַחֲרַבְתִּי֙ אֶת־ יַמָּ֔הּ וְהֹבַשְׁתִּ֖י אֶת־ מְקוֹרָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Babylon will become a heap of rubble, a haunt for jackals, an object of horror and scorn, without inhabitant.
passages.sermon:
Babylon will become a heap of rubble.
Jackals will live there.
People will see Babylon and feel horror.
People will mock Babylon.
No one will live in Babylon.
passages.original: וְהָיְתָה֩ בָבֶ֨ל׀ לְגַלִּ֧ים׀ מְעוֹן־ תַּנִּ֛ים שַׁמָּ֥ה וּשְׁרֵקָ֖ה מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵֽׁב׃

passages.text: They will roar together like young lions; they will growl like lion cubs.
passages.sermon: The people of Babylon will act together.\r\nThey will roar like young lions.\r\nThey will growl like lion cubs.
passages.original: יַחְדָּ֖ו כַּכְּפִרִ֣ים יִשְׁאָ֑גוּ נָעֲר֖וּ כְּגוֹרֵ֥י אֲרָיֽוֹת׃

passages.text: While they are flushed with heat, I will serve them a feast, and I will make them drunk so that they may revel; then they will fall asleep forever and never wake up, declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD will act against Babylon.
Babylon’s people will feel hot and restless.
The LORD will give them a feast.
The LORD will make them drunk.
They will celebrate and rejoice.
Then they will fall into a deep sleep.
They will never wake up again.
The LORD declares this.
passages.original: בְּחֻמָּ֞ם אָשִׁ֣ית אֶת־ מִשְׁתֵּיהֶ֗ם וְהִשְׁכַּרְתִּים֙ לְמַ֣עַן יַעֲלֹ֔זוּ וְיָשְׁנ֥וּ שְׁנַת־ עוֹלָ֖ם וְלֹ֣א יָקִ֑יצוּ נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams with male goats.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about Babylon’s leaders.
God says, “I will bring them down.
They will go down like lambs go to the slaughter.
They will fall like rams and male goats led to be killed.”
passages.original: אֽוֹרִידֵ֖ם כְּכָרִ֣ים לִטְב֑וֹחַ כְּאֵילִ֖ים עִם־ עַתּוּדִֽים׃

passages.text: How Sheshach has been captured! The praise of all the earth has been seized. What a horror Babylon has become among the nations!
passages.sermon:
Babylon was a great city.
People called Babylon "the praise of all the earth."
God allowed Babylon to be captured.
Sheshach is another name for Babylon.
Enemies seized Babylon.
Babylon became a horror among the nations.
People saw Babylon's fall and were shocked.
passages.original: אֵ֚יךְ נִלְכְּדָ֣ה שֵׁשַׁ֔ךְ וַתִּתָּפֵ֖שׂ תְּהִלַּ֣ת כָּל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ אֵ֣יךְ הָיְתָ֧ה לְשַׁמָּ֛ה בָּבֶ֖ל בַּגּוֹיִֽם׃

passages.text: The sea has come up over Babylon; she is covered in turbulent waves.
passages.sermon:
Babylon was a great city.
Babylon was powerful among the nations.
The sea rose up over Babylon.
Many strong waves covered her.
Babylon became overwhelmed by these waves.
passages.original: עָלָ֥ה עַל־ בָּבֶ֖ל הַיָּ֑ם בַּהֲמ֥וֹן גַּלָּ֖יו נִכְסָֽתָה׃

passages.text: Her cities have become a desolation, a dry and arid land, a land where no one lives, where no son of man passes through.
passages.sermon:
Babylon was once a great city.
Now her cities are empty.
Her cities have become a desolation.
The land is dry.
The land is arid.
No one lives there.
No person passes through.
No son of man walks there.
passages.original: הָי֤וּ עָרֶ֙יהָ֙ לְשַׁמָּ֔ה אֶ֖רֶץ צִיָּ֣ה וַעֲרָבָ֑ה אֶ֗רֶץ לֹֽא־ יֵשֵׁ֤ב בָּהֵן֙ כָּל־ אִ֔ישׁ וְלֹֽא־ יַעֲבֹ֥ר בָּהֵ֖ן בֶּן־ אָדָֽם׃

passages.text: I will punish Bel in Babylon. I will make him spew out what he swallowed. The nations will no longer stream to him; even the wall of Babylon will fall.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about Babylon.
God says He will punish Bel.
Bel is the main idol in Babylon.
God will force Bel to give up what he swallowed.
The nations will not come to Bel anymore.
The wall of Babylon will fall.
passages.original: וּפָקַדְתִּ֨י עַל־ בֵּ֜ל בְּבָבֶ֗ל וְהֹצֵאתִ֤י אֶת־ בִּלְעוֹ֙ מִפִּ֔יו וְלֹֽא־ יִנְהֲר֥וּ אֵלָ֛יו ע֖וֹד גּוֹיִ֑ם גַּם־ חוֹמַ֥ת בָּבֶ֖ל נָפָֽלָה׃

passages.text: Come out of her, My people! Save your lives, each of you, from the fierce anger of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God calls His people "My people."
God commands His people to leave Babylon.
God says, "Come out of her."
God tells each person to save his own life.
God warns of His fierce anger.
God says, "Save your lives from the fierce anger of the LORD."
passages.original: צְא֤וּ מִתּוֹכָהּ֙ עַמִּ֔י וּמַלְּט֖וּ אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־ נַפְשׁ֑וֹ מֵחֲר֖וֹן אַף־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Do not let your heart grow faint, and do not be afraid when the rumor is heard in the land; for a rumor will come one year— and then another the next year— of violence in the land and of ruler against ruler.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people in Babylon.
He warns them about coming trouble.
Do not let your heart become weak.
Do not be afraid when you hear a rumor in the land.
One year, a rumor will come.
The next year, another rumor will come.
There will be violence in the land.
One ruler will fight against another ruler.
passages.original: וּפֶן־ יֵרַ֤ךְ לְבַבְכֶם֙ וְתִֽירְא֔וּ בַּשְּׁמוּעָ֖ה הַנִּשְׁמַ֣עַת בָּאָ֑רֶץ וּבָ֧א בַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁמוּעָ֗ה וְאַחֲרָ֤יו בַּשָּׁנָה֙ הַשְּׁמוּעָ֔ה וְחָמָ֣ס בָּאָ֔רֶץ וּמֹשֵׁ֖ל עַל־ מֹשֵֽׁל׃

passages.text: Therefore, behold, the days are coming when I will punish the idols of Babylon. Her entire land will suffer shame, and all her slain will lie fallen within her.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about Babylon.
God says, “The days are coming.”
I will punish the idols of Babylon.
Babylon’s whole land will feel shame.
All the people killed in Babylon will lie dead inside her.
passages.original: לָכֵן֙ הִנֵּ֣ה יָמִ֣ים בָּאִ֔ים וּפָקַדְתִּי֙ עַל־ פְּסִילֵ֣י בָבֶ֔ל וְכָל־ אַרְצָ֖הּ תֵּב֑וֹשׁ וְכָל־ חֲלָלֶ֖יהָ יִפְּל֥וּ בְתוֹכָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Then heaven and earth and all that is in them will shout for joy over Babylon because the destroyers from the north will come against her,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
God speaks this message.
Heaven will rejoice over Babylon.
Earth will rejoice over Babylon.
Everything in heaven and earth will rejoice over Babylon.
The destroyers will come against Babylon from the north.
The LORD declares this.
passages.original: וְרִנְּנ֤וּ עַל־ בָּבֶל֙ שָׁמַ֣יִם וָאָ֔רֶץ וְכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּהֶ֑ם כִּ֧י מִצָּפ֛וֹן יָבוֹא־ לָ֥הּ הַשּׁוֹדְדִ֖ים נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: “Babylon must fall on account of the slain of Israel, just as the slain of all the earth have fallen because of Babylon.
passages.sermon:
Babylon is a great city.
Babylon has killed many people from Israel.
Babylon must fall because of the people from Israel who died.
People from many nations have also died because of Babylon.
Babylon will fall just as these people have fallen.
passages.original: גַּם־ בָּבֶ֕ל לִנְפֹּ֖ל חַֽלְלֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל גַּם־ לְבָבֶ֥ל נָפְל֖וּ חַֽלְלֵ֥י כָל־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: You who have escaped the sword, depart and do not linger! Remember the LORD from far away, and let Jerusalem come to mind.”
passages.sermon:
You have escaped the sword.
Go now.
Do not stay here.
Remember the LORD, even when you are far away.
Let Jerusalem fill your heart.
passages.original: פְּלֵטִ֣ים מֵחֶ֔רֶב הִלְכ֖וּ אַֽל־ תַּעֲמֹ֑דוּ זִכְר֤וּ מֵֽרָחוֹק֙ אֶת־ יְהוָ֔ה וִירֽוּשָׁלִַ֖ם תַּעֲלֶ֥ה עַל־ לְבַבְכֶֽם׃

passages.text: “We are ashamed because we have heard reproach; disgrace has covered our faces, because foreigners have entered the holy places of the LORD’s house.”
passages.sermon:
We are ashamed.
We have heard reproach.
Disgrace has covered our faces.
Foreigners have entered the holy places of the LORD’s house.
passages.original: בֹּ֚שְׁנוּ כִּֽי־ שָׁמַ֣עְנוּ חֶרְפָּ֔ה כִּסְּתָ֥ה כְלִמָּ֖ה פָּנֵ֑ינוּ כִּ֚י בָּ֣אוּ זָרִ֔ים עַֽל־ מִקְדְּשֵׁ֖י בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: “Therefore, behold, the days are coming,” declares the LORD, “when I will punish her idols, and throughout her land the wounded will groan.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
He says, “The days are coming.
I will punish the idols of Babylon.
Wounded people will groan in all her land.”
passages.original: לָכֵ֞ן הִנֵּֽה־ יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה וּפָקַדְתִּ֖י עַל־ פְּסִילֶ֑יהָ וּבְכָל־ אַרְצָ֖הּ יֶאֱנֹ֥ק חָלָֽל׃

passages.text: Even if Babylon ascends to the heavens and fortifies her lofty stronghold, the destroyers I send will come against her,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD is powerful and just.
Babylon is a great city.
Babylon may try to rise as high as the heavens.
Babylon may make her stronghold very secure and high.
Babylon may trust in her own strength.
But the LORD will act.
The LORD will send destroyers against Babylon.
The LORD declares this will happen.
No matter how high or strong Babylon becomes, the LORD’s destroyers will come.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ תַעֲלֶ֤ה בָבֶל֙ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְכִ֥י תְבַצֵּ֖ר מְר֣וֹם עֻזָּ֑הּ מֵאִתִּ֗י יָבֹ֧אוּ שֹׁדְדִ֛ים לָ֖הּ נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: “The sound of a cry comes from Babylon, the sound of great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans!
passages.sermon: Babylon is a great city in the land of the Chaldeans.\r\nA loud cry comes from Babylon.\r\nThere is a sound of great destruction in the land of the Chaldeans.
passages.original: ק֥וֹל זְעָקָ֖ה מִבָּבֶ֑ל וְשֶׁ֥בֶר גָּד֖וֹל מֵאֶ֥רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּֽים׃

passages.text: For the LORD will destroy Babylon; He will silence her mighty voice. The waves will roar like great waters; the tumult of their voices will resound.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
\r\nThe LORD will destroy Babylon.
\r\nBabylon is a powerful city.
\r\nBabylon has a mighty voice.
\r\nThe LORD will silence Babylon’s mighty voice.
\r\nThe people of Babylon will be like roaring waves.
\r\nThe waves will roar like great waters.
\r\nThe noise of their voices will be loud.
\r\nThe tumult of their voices will resound.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ שֹׁדֵ֤ד יְהוָה֙ אֶת־ בָּבֶ֔ל וְאִבַּ֥ד מִמֶּ֖נָּה ק֣וֹל גָּד֑וֹל וְהָמ֤וּ גַלֵּיהֶם֙ כְּמַ֣יִם רַבִּ֔ים נִתַּ֥ן שְׁא֖וֹן קוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: For a destroyer is coming against her— against Babylon. Her warriors will be captured, and their bows will be broken, for the LORD is a God of retribution; He will repay in full.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is a God of retribution.
He repays in full.
A destroyer is coming against Babylon.
Babylon’s warriors will be captured.
Their bows will be broken.
passages.original: כִּי֩ בָ֨א עָלֶ֤יהָ עַל־ בָּבֶל֙ שׁוֹדֵ֔ד וְנִלְכְּדוּ֙ גִּבּוֹרֶ֔יהָ חִתְּתָ֖ה קַשְּׁתוֹתָ֑ם כִּ֣י אֵ֧ל גְּמֻל֛וֹת יְהוָ֖ה שַׁלֵּ֥ם יְשַׁלֵּֽם׃

passages.text: I will make her princes and wise men drunk, along with her governors, officials, and warriors. Then they will fall asleep forever and not wake up,” declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is the King.
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
The LORD of Hosts will act against Babylon.
The LORD of Hosts will make Babylon’s princes drunk.
The LORD of Hosts will make Babylon’s wise men drunk.
The LORD of Hosts will make Babylon’s governors drunk.
The LORD of Hosts will make Babylon’s officials drunk.
The LORD of Hosts will make Babylon’s warriors drunk.
They will fall into a sleep that lasts forever.
They will not wake up.
passages.original: וְ֠הִשְׁכַּרְתִּי שָׂרֶ֨יהָ וַחֲכָמֶ֜יהָ פַּחוֹתֶ֤יהָ וּסְגָנֶ֙יהָ֙ וְגִבּוֹרֶ֔יהָ וְיָשְׁנ֥וּ שְׁנַת־ עוֹלָ֖ם וְלֹ֣א יָקִ֑יצוּ נְאֻ֨ם־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Babylon’s thick walls will be leveled, and her high gates consumed by fire. So the labor of the people will be for nothing; the nations will exhaust themselves to fuel the flames.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
The LORD of Hosts is the God who commands heavenly armies.
Babylon has thick walls.
These walls will be torn down.
Babylon has high gates.
Fire will burn these gates.
People from many nations will work hard.
Their work will be useless.
Nations will wear themselves out to feed the fire.
They will become tired and exhausted.
passages.original: כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת חֹ֠מוֹת בָּבֶ֤ל הָֽרְחָבָה֙ עַרְעֵ֣ר תִּתְעַרְעָ֔ר וּשְׁעָרֶ֥יהָ הַגְּבֹהִ֖ים בָּאֵ֣שׁ יִצַּ֑תּוּ וְיִֽגְע֨וּ עַמִּ֧ים בְּדֵי־ רִ֛יק וּלְאֻמִּ֥ים בְּדֵי־ אֵ֖שׁ וְיָעֵֽפוּ׃ס

passages.text: This is the message that Jeremiah the prophet gave to the quartermaster Seraiah son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah, when he went to Babylon with King Zedekiah of Judah in the fourth year of Zedekiah’s reign.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah was a prophet.
Seraiah was the son of Neriah.
Neriah was the son of Mahseiah.
Seraiah was the quartermaster.
King Zedekiah ruled Judah.
This happened in the fourth year of Zedekiah’s reign.
Seraiah went to Babylon with King Zedekiah.
Jeremiah gave a message to Seraiah at that time.
passages.original: הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר־ צִוָּ֣ה׀ יִרְמְיָ֣הוּ הַנָּבִ֗יא אֶת־ שְׂרָיָ֣ה בֶן־ נֵרִיָּה֮ בֶּן־ מַחְסֵיָה֒ בְּלֶכְתּ֞וֹ אֶת־ צִדְקִיָּ֤הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָה֙ בָּבֶ֔ל בִּשְׁנַ֥ת הָרְבִעִ֖ית לְמָלְכ֑וֹ וּשְׂרָיָ֖ה שַׂ֥ר מְנוּחָֽה׃

passages.text: Jeremiah had written on a single scroll about all the disaster that would come upon Babylon—all these words that had been written concerning Babylon.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah was a prophet.
\r\nJeremiah wrote about Babylon.
\r\nHe wrote about disaster that would come to Babylon.
\r\nHe wrote all these words on one scroll.
\r\nThese words described what would happen to Babylon.
passages.original: וַיִּכְתֹּ֣ב יִרְמְיָ֗הוּ אֵ֧ת כָּל־ הָרָעָ֛ה אֲשֶׁר־ תָּב֥וֹא אֶל־ בָּבֶ֖ל אֶל־ סֵ֣פֶר אֶחָ֑ד אֵ֚ת כָּל־ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה הַכְּתֻבִ֖ים אֶל־ בָּבֶֽל׃

passages.text: And Jeremiah said to Seraiah, “When you get to Babylon, see that you read all these words aloud, and say, ‘O LORD, You have promised to cut off this place so that no one will remain—neither man nor beast. Indeed, it will be desolate forever.’
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah was a prophet of God.
Seraiah was the son of Neriah and the son of Mahseiah.
Jeremiah spoke to Seraiah.
Jeremiah gave Seraiah a message from God.
Jeremiah said, “When you arrive in Babylon, look at the city.
Read all these words aloud in Babylon.
Say, ‘O LORD, You have spoken about this place.
You have promised to destroy it.
No one will live here.
No person will remain.
No animal will remain.
This place will be empty forever.’”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ אֶל־ שְׂרָיָ֑ה כְּבֹאֲךָ֣ בָבֶ֔ל וְֽרָאִ֔יתָ וְֽקָרָ֔אתָ אֵ֥ת כָּל־ הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃ וְאָמַרְתָּ֗ יְהוָה֙ אַתָּ֨ה דִבַּ֜רְתָּ אֶל־ הַמָּק֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ לְהַכְרִית֔וֹ לְבִלְתִּ֤י הֱיֽוֹת־ בּוֹ֙ יוֹשֵׁ֔ב לְמֵאָדָ֖ם וְעַד־ בְּהֵמָ֑ה כִּֽי־ שִׁמְמ֥וֹת עוֹלָ֖ם תִּֽהְיֶֽה׃

passages.text: When you finish reading this scroll, tie a stone to it and cast it into the Euphrates.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah was a prophet of the LORD.
Jeremiah spoke to Seraiah.
Jeremiah gave Seraiah a scroll.
The scroll contained words about Babylon’s coming disaster.
Jeremiah told Seraiah to read the scroll aloud in Babylon.
Jeremiah gave Seraiah a command.
He said, “When you finish reading this scroll, do something.”
He said, “Tie a stone to the scroll.”
He said, “Throw the scroll into the Euphrates River.”
passages.original: וְהָיָה֙ כְּכַלֹּ֣תְךָ֔ לִקְרֹ֖א אֶת־ הַסֵּ֣פֶר הַזֶּ֑ה תִּקְשֹׁ֤ר עָלָיו֙ אֶ֔בֶן וְהִשְׁלַכְתּ֖וֹ אֶל־ תּ֥וֹךְ פְּרָֽת׃

passages.text: Then you are to say, ‘In the same way Babylon will sink and never rise again, because of the disaster I will bring upon her. And her people will grow weary.’ ” Here end the words of Jeremiah.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah was a prophet of the LORD.
Jeremiah spoke to Seraiah.
Jeremiah gave Seraiah a message from God.
Jeremiah said, "Babylon will sink like this scroll in the river."
Babylon will not rise again.
God will bring disaster on Babylon.
The people of Babylon will become tired and weak.
These are the last words Jeremiah spoke in this message.
passages.original: וְאָמַרְתָּ֗ כָּ֠כָה תִּשְׁקַ֨ע בָּבֶ֤ל וְלֹֽא־ תָקוּם֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י הָרָעָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר אָנֹכִ֛י מֵבִ֥יא עָלֶ֖יהָ וְיָעֵ֑פוּ עַד־ הֵ֖נָּה דִּבְרֵ֥י יִרְמְיָֽהוּ׃ס
